description: Task 4.1 Security Hardening (CRITICAL). Input sanitization for user-supplied paths (CLI + dashboard trace files), full audit + documentation of every unsafe block in xplainit-c (FFI) and xplainit-java (JNI), FFI boundary safety checks, and secrets/PII redaction of captured trace values (opt-out by default-safe policy). Dependency audit is performed by available means since cargo audit is unavailable offline. Establish the green baseline before making changes.
steps: Create branch phase4-production-hardening off master (git checkout -b phase4-production-hardening). Confirm baseline green FIRST: cargo build --release; cargo test; cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings; cargo fmt --all -- --check; and the four Python suites (see context.json test_command). Record baseline test count.

Input sanitization for trace/log file paths: add a small path-validation helper in xplainit-core (e.g. a new module xplainit-core/src/security.rs exporting a function like validate_input_path(&Path) -> Result that rejects clearly hostile inputs: empty paths, NUL bytes in the path, and non-existent/non-file targets before opening) and wire it into the file-loading paths used by xplainit-cli/src/commands/analyze.rs, report.rs, explain.rs and xplainit-dashboard/src/trace.rs. Keep behavior backward compatible for valid files. Do NOT block legitimate relative/absolute paths the user intends; the goal is validation and clear errors, not lockout.

Audit unsafe blocks: read every unsafe block in xplainit-c/src/*.rs (23) and xplainit-java/src/*.rs (10). For each, add a `// SAFETY:` doc comment immediately above it explaining the invariants that make it sound (pointer non-null/alignment/lifetime, valid UTF-8 assumptions, ownership/free responsibility across the FFI boundary). Add explicit null-pointer / length guards where a raw pointer or length is dereferenced without a check (return an error code or safe default instead of UB). Do not change the public FFI ABI/signatures.

Secrets/PII redaction: add redaction configuration to xplainit-core/src/config.rs (e.g. a `redact_secrets: bool` defaulting to true and a `redact_key_patterns: Vec<String>` defaulting to common secret-like names: password, passwd, secret, token, api_key, apikey, authorization, auth, credential, private_key). Implement redaction where named runtime values are captured or rendered: when a variable/argument key case-insensitively matches a redaction pattern, replace its Value with a redacted placeholder (e.g. Value::String("<redacted>")) in the formatter/serialization path (xplainit-core/src/formatter.rs and any JSON serialization used for traces). Ensure redaction is applied before values leave the process (console output, JSON, dashboard payloads). Provide a helper so bindings/CLI benefit without duplicating logic.

Dependency audit by available means (cargo audit is UNAVAILABLE offline): do NOT attempt to install or run cargo audit/cargo outdated/cargo-vet. Instead, add a docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md documenting: the dependency set (from Cargo.lock), that versions are pinned via Cargo.lock, that automated advisory scanning (cargo audit) and supply-chain attestation (cargo-vet) are blocked by the offline INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox, and the exact commands a maintainer should run when online. Do not fabricate advisory results.

Add revert-sensitive tests: unit tests for validate_input_path (rejects empty/NUL, accepts a real temp file, errors on missing file); unit tests for redaction (a value under key 'password'/'api_key' is redacted; a normal key like 'count' is not; case-insensitivity works); and tests asserting the SAFETY-guarded FFI functions return the safe error path when given a null pointer (where the C/Java crates are testable in-process). Place Rust tests in the relevant crate test modules; add an integration test in xplainit-core/tests for redaction end-to-end through serialization.
Run the full gate set and all four Python suites; fix any clippy/fmt issues introduced. Commit on the branch: `feat: security hardening - input validation, unsafe audit, secret redaction (FEAT-001)`.
acceptance_criteria: A path-validation helper exists in xplainit-core and is called by the CLI trace/log loaders and the dashboard trace loader; invalid inputs (empty, NUL byte, missing file) produce a clear error instead of a panic or UB.
Every unsafe block in xplainit-c and xplainit-java has a // SAFETY: comment, and raw-pointer/length dereferences have explicit guards.

Config exposes redaction settings defaulting to on; captured values whose key matches a secret-like pattern are replaced with a redacted placeholder in console/JSON/dashboard output, verified by tests.
docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md documents the dependency audit approach and states clearly which tooling is blocked offline and the commands to run when online (no fabricated advisory output).
cargo build --release, cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo fmt --all -- --check all pass; the four Python suites still pass.
New tests fail if the corresponding code (validation, redaction, FFI guards) is reverted.
verification: source .venv/bin/activate && python test_automatic_tracing.py && cd xplainit-python && maturin develop --release && python test_frame_filter.py && python test_depth_accounting.py && python test_decorators.py
Manually confirm redaction: run the CLI report/analyze over a trace JSON containing a value keyed 'password' and confirm the output shows the redacted placeholder, not the value.
findings: Implemented on branch phase4-production-hardening (off master 7ecffa0). Baseline confirmed green first: cargo build/test/clippy/fmt clean, 178 tests, Python 3/3+11/11+23/23+decorators. Changes: (1) New xplainit-core/src/security.rs with validate_input_path (rejects empty/NUL/missing/non-file) and redaction helpers (is_redaction_key, redact_named_value, DEFAULT_REDACTION_PATTERNS, REDACTED_PLACEHOLDER), re-exported from lib.rs. (2) Config gained redact_secrets:bool (default true) and redact_key_patterns:Vec<String> (default: password/passwd/secret/token/api_key/apikey/authorization/auth/credential/private_key). (3) events.rs: added ExecutionEvent::redacted(patterns) + redact_events() free fn (re-exported) that scrub secret-keyed args/variable values/RuntimeError context/stack-frame arguments, recursively into nested Object/Array values, before serialization. (4) Path validation + redaction wired into CLI load_events (xplainit-cli/src/commands/mod.rs, used by analyze/report/explain) and dashboard trace.rs. (5) Added // SAFETY: comments to all 13 unsafe operations in xplainit-c/src/lib.rs and all unsafe blocks (10) in xplainit-java/src/lib.rs; null/handle guards already existed and are documented as the safe error path. FFI ABI/signatures unchanged. (6) docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md documents dependency set from Cargo.lock (202 pinned entries), states cargo audit/cargo-vet/cargo-outdated are blocked offline (no fabricated advisories), and gives the exact online commands. Tests added (revert-sensitive): security.rs unit tests (path validation empty/NUL/missing/dir/real-file; redaction key matching + value redaction), config redaction-defaults test, C null-handle statistics/enable-disable safe-error tests, and two xplainit-core integration tests (redaction end-to-end through JSON serialization; validate_input_path). One existing CLI test (analyze_missing_file_fails) updated to expect the new clearer 'does not exist' message (still non-zero exit). Verification: cargo build --release OK; cargo test = 191 passed / 0 failed (+13 over baseline); clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --all --check clean; Python 3/3, 11/11, 23/23, decorators pass; manual CLI redaction confirmed (password value shows <redacted>, non-secret 'user' preserved). Committed on branch. Note: release profile has panic="abort" (relevant to Task 4.2). Java native null-handle guards are not unit-tested in-process because those natives require a live JNIEnv; the pure build_* event helpers remain tested.
